answer: Unique hardware pulse binding. Each identity must emit a continuous low-power radio pulse from a physically unclonable circuit; the vine of relayed signals is traced to its origin emitter, and duplicates on one chip are rejected at registration. An attacker cloning identities pays the full fabrication cost of a distinct chip per identity, since the pulse cannot be copied or simulated. A comet of forged pulses from one device collapses to a single traceable origin, capping the sybil count at hardware units actually owned.
